source.text: אַחַ֣ר׀הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־אַבְרָ֔ם בַּֽמַּחֲזֶ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אַל־תִּירָ֣א אַבְרָ֗ם אָנֹכִי֙ מָגֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ שְׂכָרְךָ֖ הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: After these things came [the] word of YHWH to Abram in a vision, saying, do not fear, Abram; I [am] a shield to you; your reward [will be] very great.

en.L: After these things the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Abram in a vision, saying, "Do not fear, Abram; I [am] a shield to you; your reward [will be] very great."
en.B: Some time later the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, and your reward will be very great."
en.R: Some time later {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Abram in a vision. He said, "Do not be afraid, Abram. I will protect you like a shield, and I will reward you greatly."

es.L: Después de estas cosas vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Abram en una visión, y dijo: «No temas, Abram; yo [soy] un escudo para ti; tu recompensa [será] muy grande».
es.B: Algún tiempo después, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a Abram en una visión: «No temas, Abram: tu escudo soy yo, y muy grande será tu recompensa».
es.R: Algún tiempo después, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le habló a Abram en una visión. Le dijo: «No tengas miedo, Abram. Yo te protegeré como un escudo, y te daré una gran recompensa».

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came ... in a vision: the language of prophecy
decisions.reason: "The word of the LORD came to" is how the prophets describe God speaking to them (Jeremiah 1:2; Hosea 1:1). Abram is later called a prophet (20:7).

decisions.choice: a shield: protection
decisions.reason: God promises protection after Abram's battle (chapter 14). The word (magen) echoes "delivered" (miggen) in 14:20.

decisions.choice: your reward will be very great
alternatives: I am your shield, your very great reward
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can mean that Abram's reward will be great, or that God himself is his very great reward. Having refused the spoils (14:22-24), Abram is promised a greater reward from God; the next verse shows he understands it as the gift of a son.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}
decisions.reason: First occurrence of the divine name in this chapter. As in 2:4, it is "el SEÑOR" in small capitals by default, with "Yahvé" as a reader setting; the span takes in the article and any contraction ("del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé").

decisions.choice: No temas (L, B); No tengas miedo (R)
decisions.reason: "No temas" is the set form of God's reassurance and is still natural in careful Spanish; Readable uses the everyday "No tengas miedo".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָ֗ם אֲדֹנָ֤י יֱהוִה֙ מַה־תִּתֶּן־לִ֔י וְאָנֹכִ֖י הוֹלֵ֣ךְ עֲרִירִ֑י וּבֶן־מֶ֣שֶׁק בֵּיתִ֔י ה֖וּא דַּמֶּ֥שֶׂק אֱלִיעֶֽזֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abram, my Lord YHWH, what will you give me, and I [am] going childless, and the heir of my house, he [is] Damascus Eliezer?

en.L: And Abram said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, what will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me, since I go on childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?"
en.B: But Abram answered, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, what will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me? I am still childless, and everything I have will go to Eliezer of Damascus."
en.R: But Abram said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, what good is any reward when I have no children? The one who will get everything I own when I die is Eliezer of Damascus."

es.L: Y dijo Abram: «{{divine_name:Señor DIOS|Señor Yahvé}}, ¿qué me darás, pues sigo sin hijos, y el heredero de mi casa es Eliezer de Damasco?».
es.B: Pero Abram respondió: «{{divine_name:Señor DIOS|Señor Yahvé}}, ¿qué me vas a dar? Sigo sin tener hijos, y todo lo que tengo pasará a Eliezer de Damasco».
es.R: Pero Abram dijo: «{{divine_name:Señor DIOS|Señor Yahvé}}, ¿de qué me sirve una recompensa si no tengo hijos? Cuando yo muera, el que se quedará con todo lo que tengo es Eliezer de Damasco».

decisions.choice: my Lord, the LORD: Adonai YHWH
decisions.reason: Abram addresses God as "my Lord" (adonai), followed by the divine name. It is the language of respectful prayer.

decisions.choice: the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus
alternatives: the son of possession of my house
decisions.reason: The phrase is obscure; it may mean "the one who will possess my house". The word for it (mesheq) sounds like Damascus (Dammeseq). The point is clear: without a son, Abram's estate will pass to a member of his household. Ancient custom allowed a childless man to adopt a servant as heir.

decisions.choice: Lord GOD (default); Lord Yahweh (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: When the divine name follows "Lord", English Bibles by long custom write "Lord GOD" in capitals, rather than "Lord LORD". The divine name setting gives "Lord Yahweh". "You" addressed to God takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:Señor DIOS|Señor Yahvé}}
decisions.reason: As in the English ("Lord GOD"), when the divine name follows "my Lord" (m1) it is written "DIOS" in capitals rather than "Señor SEÑOR"; the divine name setting gives "Señor Yahvé". The span covers both words so that the setting reads naturally.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָ֔ם הֵ֣ן לִ֔י לֹ֥א נָתַ֖תָּה זָ֑רַע וְהִנֵּ֥ה בֶן־בֵּיתִ֖י יוֹרֵ֥שׁ אֹתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abram, behold, to me not you have given offspring, and behold, a son of my house [is] inheriting me.

en.L: And Abram said, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given me no offspring, and so a member of my household will be my heir."
en.B: Abram went on, "Since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not given me a child, someone born in my household will inherit from me."
en.R: Abram said, "You have not given me any children, so one of my servants will get everything I own."

es.L: Y dijo Abram: «Mira, no me has dado descendencia, y así un miembro de mi casa será mi heredero».
es.B: Abram añadió: «Como no me has dado un hijo, alguien nacido en mi casa será quien me herede».
es.R: Abram dijo: «No me has dado hijos, así que uno de mis siervos se quedará con todo lo que tengo».

decisions.choice: a son of my house: someone born in my household
decisions.reason: "Son of my house" means a member of the household, such as a servant born there (14:14), not Abram's own child.

decisions.choice: no me has dado (no pronoun for God)
decisions.reason: The English has a deity pronoun span on "you". Spanish carries the subject in the verb ending, so there is no written pronoun and no span; adding "tú" would sound emphatic.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א יִֽירָשְׁךָ֖ זֶ֑ה כִּי־אִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵצֵ֣א מִמֵּעֶ֔יךָ ה֖וּא יִֽירָשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And behold, [the] word of YHWH [came] to him, saying, not will inherit you this [one]; but [one] who will come out from your inward parts, he will inherit you.

en.L: And look, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him: "This man will not be your heir; one who will come out from your own body, he will be your heir."
en.B: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him: "No, he will not inherit from you. Your heir will be your own son, born of your own body."
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Your servant will not get your things. You will have a son of your own, and he will get everything."

es.L: Y, mira, la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a él: «Este no será tu heredero; el que saldrá de tus propias entrañas, ese será tu heredero».
es.B: Entonces la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a él: «No, ese no te heredará. Tu heredero será un hijo tuyo, nacido de tu propio cuerpo».
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Abram: «Tu siervo no se quedará con tus cosas. Tendrás un hijo propio, y él lo recibirá todo».

decisions.choice: who will come out from your inward parts: your own son
decisions.reason: The phrase means a child of Abram's own body (2 Samuel 7:12).

decisions.choice: de tus propias entrañas (L); de tu propio cuerpo (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bodily image of the Hebrew (m1) with "entrañas", which in Spanish can still mean the body as the source of offspring; Balanced says "cuerpo", as the English does at both levels.

source.text: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א אֹת֜וֹ הַח֗וּצָה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַבֶּט־נָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֗יְמָה וּסְפֹר֙ הַכּ֣וֹכָבִ֔ים אִם־תּוּכַ֖ל לִסְפֹּ֣ר אֹתָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ כֹּ֥ה יִהְיֶ֖ה זַרְעֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought him outside and said, look, please, to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to count them. And he said to him, so will be your offspring.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought him outside and said, "Look toward the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to count them." And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "So shall your offspring be."
en.B: He led Abram outside and said, "Look up into the sky and try counting the stars, if you can." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him, "Your descendants will be like that."
en.R: Then God took Abram outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you can. You will have as many descendants as that."

es.L: Y lo llevó afuera y dijo: «Mira, por favor, a los cielos, y si eres capaz de contar las estrellas, cuéntalas». Y le dijo: «Tal será tu descendencia».
es.B: Lo llevó afuera y le dijo: «Mira al cielo e intenta contar las estrellas, si puedes». Luego añadió: «Así de numerosos serán tus descendientes».
es.R: Entonces Dios sacó a Abram afuera y le dijo: «Mira el cielo y cuenta las estrellas, si puedes. Así de numerosos serán tus descendientes, los hijos de tus hijos».

decisions.choice: count the stars: offspring beyond counting
decisions.reason: As with the dust of the earth (13:16), the promise is of numbers no one can count (22:17; Hebrews 11:12).

decisions.choice: descendencia (L); descendientes (B, R)
decisions.reason: As settled in chapter 12: the collective "descendencia" at Literal, the plural "descendientes" at Balanced and Readable. Readable adds "los hijos de tus hijos" the first time, so a young reader knows what "descendientes" means.

decisions.choice: lo llevó ... le dijo (no pronoun for God)
decisions.reason: The English has deity pronoun spans on "he"; Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ending, so there is no span. Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְהֶאֱמִ֖ן בַּֽיהוָ֑ה וַיַּחְשְׁבֶ֥הָ לּ֖וֹ צְדָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he believed in YHWH, and he counted it to him [as] righteousness.

en.L: And he believed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} counted it to him [as] righteousness.
en.B: Abram put his trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} counted it to his credit as righteousness.
en.R: Abram believed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} accepted Abram as righteous because he believed.

es.L: Y creyó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se lo acreditó [como] justicia.
es.B: Abram confió en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se lo acreditó como justicia.
es.R: Abram creyó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} aceptó a Abram como justo porque creyó.

decisions.choice: believed: trusted, relied on God's word
decisions.reason: The verb (he'emin) means to consider reliable and to lean on it: Abram took God at his word, though nothing he could see supported it.

decisions.choice: he counted it to him as righteousness: God accepted Abram as right with him
alternatives: Abram counted it (the promise) as God's righteousness
decisions.reason: The natural reading is that the LORD counted Abram's faith as righteousness. Some read Abram as the subject, counting the promise as God's justice. Paul and James both quote the verse with the first meaning (Romans 4:3; Galatians 3:6; James 2:23).

decisions.choice: righteousness: being in the right with God
decisions.reason: The word means right conduct, or standing in the right, in a right relationship (Deuteronomy 6:25). Here it is God's verdict on Abram, given because he believed.

decisions.choice: put his trust in ... counted it to his credit
alternatives: believed ... credited it to him as righteousness
decisions.reason: Balanced says "put his trust in" to bring out the sense of the verb (m1); Literal and Readable keep "believed", the word the New Testament uses when it quotes the verse.

decisions.choice: creyó (L, R), confió en (B); se lo acreditó como justicia; aceptó ... como justo (R)
decisions.reason: Galatians 3:6 and James 2:23 already quote this verse in Spanish with "creyó a Dios" and "le fue acreditado / se le acreditó como justicia", and their Readable with "lo aceptó como justo". Genesis uses the same verb and noun at each level so the reader can see that Paul and James cite this sentence. "Acreditar" is the bookkeeping word for entering something to a person's account (m2); "contar por" and "imputar" are older. Balanced "confió en" follows the English Balanced (r-en-1). Literal keeps "él" with the deity pronoun span, since the subject changes back to God (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵאתִ֨יךָ֙ מֵא֣וּר כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים לָ֧תֶת לְךָ֛ אֶת־הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, I [am] YHWH who brought you out from Ur of [the] Chaldeans to give to you this land to possess it.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess."
en.B: He also told him, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to be your own."
en.R: He also said to Abram, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I brought you out of Ur in Chaldea to give you this land to be your own."

es.L: Y le dijo: «Yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el que te sacó de Ur de los caldeos a fin de darte esta tierra en posesión».
es.B: También le dijo: «Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Yo te traje desde Ur de los caldeos para darte esta tierra como posesión tuya».
es.R: También le dijo a Abram: «Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Yo te saqué de Ur, en Caldea, para darte esta tierra. Será tuya».

decisions.choice: I am the LORD who brought you out: the words that open the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: God introduces himself as he will at Sinai: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt" (Exodus 20:2). Abram's journey from Ur is the first exodus.

source.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יֱהוִ֔ה בַּמָּ֥ה אֵדַ֖ע כִּ֥י אִֽירָשֶֽׁנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, my Lord YHWH, how will I know that I will possess it?

en.L: And he said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, how will I know that I will possess it?"
en.B: But Abram said, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, how can I be sure that I will possess it?"
en.R: But Abram asked, "{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, how can I be sure that this land will belong to me?"

es.L: Y dijo: «{{divine_name:Señor DIOS|Señor Yahvé}}, ¿cómo sabré que la poseeré?».
es.B: Pero Abram dijo: «{{divine_name:Señor DIOS|Señor Yahvé}}, ¿cómo puedo estar seguro de que la poseeré?».
es.R: Pero Abram preguntó: «{{divine_name:Señor DIOS|Señor Yahvé}}, ¿cómo puedo estar seguro de que esta tierra será mía?».

decisions.choice: how will I know: asking for a sign, not doubting
decisions.reason: Abram has just believed (verse 6). His question asks for assurance, and God answers it with a covenant.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו קְחָ֥ה לִי֙ עֶגְלָ֣ה מְשֻׁלֶּ֔שֶׁת וְעֵ֥ז מְשֻׁלֶּ֖שֶׁת וְאַ֣יִל מְשֻׁלָּ֑שׁ וְתֹ֖ר וְגוֹזָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, bring me a heifer three years old, and a goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove and a young pigeon."
en.B: He answered, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat and a three-year-old ram, with a turtledove and a young pigeon."
en.R: God said to him, "Bring me a young cow, a female goat and a ram, each three years old, and a dove and a young pigeon."

es.L: Y le dijo: «Tráeme una novilla de tres años, una cabra de tres años, un carnero de tres años, una tórtola y un pichón».
es.B: Le respondió: «Tráeme una novilla, una cabra y un carnero, todos de tres años, además de una tórtola y un pichón».
es.R: Dios le dijo: «Tráeme una vaca joven, una cabra y un carnero, cada uno de tres años, y también una tórtola y una paloma joven».

decisions.choice: the animals: those later used in Israel's sacrifices
decisions.reason: These are the kinds of animals the law of Moses later prescribes for sacrifice. Here they are used to make a covenant.

decisions.choice: una cabra (female); un pichón (L, B), una paloma joven (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "cabra" is already female, so the English "female goat" needs no extra word. "Pichón" is the ordinary word for a young pigeon; Readable says "una paloma joven" in plain words.

source.text: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֗לֶּה וַיְבַתֵּ֤ר אֹתָם֙ בַּתָּ֔וֶךְ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אִישׁ־בִּתְר֖וֹ לִקְרַ֣את רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְאֶת־הַצִפֹּ֖רלֹ֥א בָתָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought to him all these, and cut them in the middle, and set each piece opposite its neighbor; and the birds he did not cut.

en.L: And he brought him all these, and cut them in two, and laid each half opposite the other; but the birds he did not cut in two.
en.B: Abram brought them all, split each one down the middle and laid the halves facing each other, but he did not split the birds.
en.R: Abram brought all these animals, cut them in half and laid the halves in two rows facing each other. But he did not cut the birds in half.

es.L: Y le trajo todos estos, y los partió por el medio, y puso cada mitad frente a la otra; pero las aves no las partió.
es.B: Abram se los trajo todos, partió cada animal por la mitad y colocó las mitades una frente a otra, pero no partió las aves.
es.R: Abram le trajo todos esos animales, los cortó en dos y puso las mitades en dos filas, una frente a otra. Pero a las aves no las cortó.

decisions.choice: cut in two, each half opposite the other: a covenant ritual
decisions.reason: In an ancient covenant the parties walked between the halves of slaughtered animals, as if to say "may I be cut in two like these if I break this covenant" (Jeremiah 34:18-20). Hebrew speaks of "cutting" a covenant (verse 18).

source.text: וַיֵּ֥רֶד הָעַ֖יִט עַל־הַפְּגָרִ֑ים וַיַּשֵּׁ֥ב אֹתָ֖ם אַבְרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came down the birds of prey on the carcasses, and drove them away Abram.

en.L: And birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
en.B: When birds of prey swooped down on the carcasses, Abram chased them off.
en.R: Vultures came down to eat the dead animals, but Abram chased them away.

es.L: Y bajaron las aves de rapiña sobre los cadáveres, y Abram las ahuyentó.
es.B: Las aves de rapiña se lanzaron sobre los cadáveres, pero Abram las espantó.
es.R: Unos buitres bajaron a comerse los animales muertos, pero Abram los espantó.

decisions.choice: birds of prey: a threat to the covenant
decisions.reason: Abram guards the offering. Some see in the birds a picture of the threats to the promise; the text does not explain them.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ לָב֔וֹא וְתַרְדֵּמָ֖ה נָפְלָ֣ה עַל־אַבְרָ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵימָ֛ה חֲשֵׁכָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה נֹפֶ֥לֶת עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, the sun [was] about to go, and a deep sleep fell on Abram; and behold, dread, darkness great, falling on him.

en.L: And as the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram; and look, a dread and great darkness fell on him.
en.B: When the sun was going down, a deep sleep came over Abram, and with it a great and terrifying darkness.
en.R: As the sun was going down, Abram fell into a deep sleep. A terrible darkness came over him, and he was very afraid.

es.L: Y cuando el sol estaba por ponerse, un sueño profundo cayó sobre Abram; y, mira, un espanto y una gran oscuridad cayeron sobre él.
es.B: Cuando el sol se estaba poniendo, un sueño profundo se apoderó de Abram, y con él una oscuridad densa y aterradora.
es.R: Cuando el sol se estaba poniendo, Abram se quedó profundamente dormido. Una oscuridad terrible lo cubrió, y sintió mucho miedo.

decisions.choice: a deep sleep: the sleep of 2:21
decisions.reason: The word is the one used when God made the woman from the man (2:21): a sleep sent by God, in which he acts or speaks.

decisions.choice: dread, great darkness: terror at God's presence
decisions.reason: The dread is the fear that comes with God's nearness, and perhaps a foretaste of the dark years he is about to announce.

decisions.choice: un sueño profundo (L, B); se quedó profundamente dormido (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as the Spanish of 2:21 at each level, so the echo the meaning decision points to (m1) is kept.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאַבְרָ֗ם יָדֹ֨עַ תֵּדַ֜ע כִּי־גֵ֣ר׀יִהְיֶ֣ה זַרְעֲךָ֗ בְּאֶ֨רֶץ֙ לֹ֣א לָהֶ֔ם וַעֲבָד֖וּם וְעִנּ֣וּ אֹתָ֑ם אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to Abram, knowing you shall know that a sojourner will be your offspring in a land not theirs, and they will serve them and they will afflict them four hundred years.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Abram, "Know for certain that your offspring will be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and they will be slaves there and be afflicted for 400 years.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "You must understand that your descendants will be foreigners in a land that is not theirs. They will be enslaved and oppressed for 400 years.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "I want you to know that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that does not belong to them. The people there will make them slaves and treat them badly for 400 years.

es.L: Entonces dijo a Abram: «Sabe con certeza que tu descendencia será extranjera en una tierra que no es suya, y allí servirán como esclavos y serán oprimidos durante 400 años.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Abram: «Debes saber que tus descendientes serán extranjeros en una tierra que no es suya. Allí los esclavizarán y los oprimirán durante 400 años.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Abram: «Quiero que sepas que tus descendientes vivirán como extranjeros en un país que no es de ellos. La gente de allí los hará esclavos y los tratará mal durante 400 años.

decisions.choice: a land not theirs, slaves, afflicted: the years in Egypt
decisions.reason: God foretells Israel's slavery in Egypt (Exodus 1:11-12), using the words of the exodus story: "serve" and "afflict".

decisions.choice: 400 years: a round number
decisions.reason: Exodus 12:40 gives 430 years; Acts 7:6 repeats 400. The number is a round figure for the long stay. Verse 16 counts it as four generations.

decisions.choice: the LORD said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker; Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: extranjera (L), extranjeros (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means a resident foreigner without rights in the land. "Extranjero" says this plainly at every level; "peregrino" now suggests a pilgrim. At Literal the adjective agrees with the collective "descendencia".

source.text: וְגַ֧ם אֶת־הַגּ֛וֹי אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲבֹ֖דוּ דָּ֣ן אָנֹ֑כִי וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֥ן יֵצְא֖וּ בִּרְכֻ֥שׁ גָּדֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And also the nation that they will serve I will judge, and afterward they will come out with possessions great.

en.L: But I will judge the nation that they serve, and afterward they will come out with great possessions.
en.B: But I will bring judgment on the nation that enslaves them, and afterward they will come out with great wealth.
en.R: But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves. Afterward your descendants will leave that land with great riches.

es.L: Pero también a la nación a la que sirvan, yo la juzgaré, y después saldrán con grandes posesiones.
es.B: Pero yo traeré juicio sobre la nación que los esclavice, y después saldrán de allí con grandes riquezas.
es.R: Pero yo castigaré a la nación que los haga esclavos. Después, tus descendientes saldrán de ese país con muchas riquezas.

decisions.choice: judge: bring judgment on
decisions.reason: God will judge the nation, Egypt, by the plagues (Exodus 6:6; 12:12). The "great possessions" recall Israel leaving Egypt with gifts from the Egyptians (Exodus 12:35-36).

source.text: וְאַתָּ֛ה תָּב֥וֹא אֶל־אֲבֹתֶ֖יךָ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם תִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּשֵׂיבָ֥ה טוֹבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, you will go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried in old age good.

en.L: As for you, you will go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age.
en.B: As for you, you will join your ancestors in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.
en.R: But you will die in peace when you are very old and be buried.

es.L: Y tú irás a tus padres en paz; serás sepultado en buena vejez.
es.B: En cuanto a ti, te reunirás en paz con tus antepasados y serás sepultado tras una vejez dichosa.
es.R: Pero tú morirás en paz cuando seas muy anciano, y te enterrarán.

decisions.choice: go to your fathers: die, and join those who died before
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks of death as joining one's ancestors (25:8). Abram himself will not see the slavery or the return.

source.text: וְד֥וֹר רְבִיעִ֖י יָשׁ֣וּבוּ הֵ֑נָּה כִּ֧י לֹא־שָׁלֵ֛ם עֲוֺ֥ן הָאֱמֹרִ֖י עַד־הֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] generation fourth will return here, for not complete [is the] iniquity of the Amorite[s] until now.

en.L: And in the fourth generation they will come back here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete."
en.B: Your descendants will return here in the fourth generation, because the Amorites' wickedness has not yet run its full course."
en.R: After four generations your descendants will come back here. I will wait until then, because the Amorites who live here have not yet become so evil that they must be punished."

es.L: Y la cuarta generación volverá acá, porque aún no está completa la iniquidad de los amorreos».
es.B: Tus descendientes volverán aquí en la cuarta generación, porque la maldad de los amorreos todavía no ha llegado a su límite».
es.R: Después de cuatro generaciones, tus descendientes volverán aquí. Esperaré hasta entonces, porque los amorreos que viven aquí todavía no se han vuelto tan malos como para merecer el castigo».

decisions.choice: the fourth generation: a long lifetime-length period
decisions.reason: A generation here may be a long period (about a hundred years), matching the 400 years of verse 13.

decisions.choice: the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete: God's patience and justice
decisions.reason: God will give the land to Abram's descendants only when its people's sin has reached its full measure (Leviticus 18:24-28). The delay shows both his patience with the Amorites and the justice of the later conquest.

decisions.choice: I will wait until then, because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the delay means (m2).

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ בָּ֔אָה וַעֲלָטָ֖ה הָיָ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה תַנּ֤וּר עָשָׁן֙ וְלַפִּ֣יד אֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָבַ֔ר בֵּ֖ין הַגְּזָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, the sun had gone and darkness was, and behold, a pot of smoke and a torch of fire which passed between these pieces.

en.L: And when the sun had gone down and it was dark, look, a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between these pieces.
en.B: After sunset, in the dark, a smoking fire pot and a blazing torch passed between the halves of the animals.
en.R: After the sun had gone down and it was dark, a pot full of smoke and a burning torch appeared. They moved between the halves of the animals.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando el sol se había puesto y estaba oscuro, mira, un brasero humeante y una antorcha de fuego pasaron entre estos pedazos.
es.B: Cuando ya se había puesto el sol y todo estaba oscuro, un brasero humeante y una antorcha encendida pasaron entre las mitades de los animales.
es.R: Cuando el sol ya se había puesto y estaba oscuro, aparecieron un brasero que echaba humo y una antorcha encendida. Pasaron entre las mitades de los animales.

decisions.choice: a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch: signs of God's presence
decisions.reason: Smoke and fire mark God's presence, as later at Sinai and in the pillar of cloud and fire (Exodus 13:21; 19:18).

decisions.choice: passed between these pieces: God alone binds himself
decisions.reason: Only God's presence passes between the pieces; Abram does not. God takes the whole obligation of the covenant on himself, as if to say "may I be torn apart if I do not keep my word".

decisions.choice: un brasero humeante (L, B); un brasero que echaba humo (R)
decisions.reason: The object is a portable clay pot holding fire. "Brasero" names a container of live coals and is understood everywhere; "horno" suggests a large fixed oven, and "olla" a cooking pot without fire.

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא כָּרַ֧ת יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־אַבְרָ֖ם בְּרִ֣ית לֵאמֹ֑ר לְזַרְעֲךָ֗ נָתַ֨תִּי֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את מִנְּהַ֣ר מִצְרַ֔יִם עַד־הַנָּהָ֥ר הַגָּדֹ֖ל נְהַר־פְּרָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: On that day cut YHWH with Abram a covenant, saying, to your offspring I give this land, from [the] river of Egypt to the river the great, [the] river Euphrates,

en.L: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your offspring I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
en.B: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with Abram: "I am giving this land to your descendants, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates,
en.R: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made a covenant with Abram. He said, "I am giving this land to your descendants, from the river at the border of Egypt to the great Euphrates River.

es.L: En aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo un pacto con Abram, y dijo: «A tu descendencia doy esta tierra, del río de Egipto al río grande, el río Éufrates:
es.B: Aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo un pacto con Abram: «A tus descendientes les doy esta tierra, que se extiende del río de Egipto al gran río Éufrates,
es.R: Aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo un pacto con Abram. Le dijo: «Les doy a tus descendientes esta tierra, desde el río que está en la frontera de Egipto hasta el gran río Éufrates.

decisions.choice: cut a covenant: made a covenant
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "cut" a covenant, from the ritual of cutting animals (verse 10).

decisions.choice: I give: a gift made as God speaks
decisions.reason: The completed verb form announces the gift as settled, as in 1:29 and 9:13.

decisions.choice: from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates: the widest borders of the land
decisions.reason: "The river of Egypt" may be the Nile or, more likely, the wadi on Egypt's border with Canaan (Numbers 34:5). The borders reached their fullest under David and Solomon (1 Kings 4:21).

es.B: la tierra de los quenitas, quenizitas, cadmoneos,
es.R: Es la tierra de los quenitas, los quenizitas, los cadmoneos,

decisions.choice: ten peoples: the whole population of the land
decisions.reason: The list of ten peoples (verses 19-21) is the longest of its kind, a way of saying "everyone who lived there".

decisions.choice: quenitas, quenizitas, cadmoneos (verses 19-21: hititas, ferezeos, refaítas, amorreos, cananeos, gergeseos, jebuseos)
decisions.reason: Gentilics are lower case. Peoples already named in the Spanish of chapter 10 keep those forms (jebuseos, amorreos, gergeseos, cananeos); "ferezeos" and "refaítas" are the usual Spanish forms. For the less familiar names the modern forms "quenitas" and "quenizitas" are used, and "hititas", the name readers know from history, rather than the older "heteos".

decisions.choice: Es la tierra de ...
alternatives: la tierra de ... (as the English Readable)
decisions.reason: The English Readable ends verse 18 with a full stop and continues the list in lower case. Spanish Readable makes verse 19 a short sentence of its own with "Es".
